text: The model flagged the applicant as high‑risk because of three key signals it examined. First, the applicant’s revolving‑credit utilization is essentially 100 % of the available limit; using almost all of the credit pushes the risk score upward sharply. Second, the applicant’s age of 30 contributes additional risk, as younger borrowers in this data set tend to default more often. Third, the applicant has only one open credit line or loan, which slightly pulls the risk score down, but this modest offset is not enough to outweigh the strong negative impact of the near‑full credit usage and the age factor. Together, these influences lead the model to assign a 61.3 % probability of default.
